# The workflow engine this project builds its loop framework on. Vendored as the
# `vendor/tinyflows` submodule and pinned by its gitlink, the same arrangement
# TinyBus uses. It is host-agnostic by construction — every effect goes through
# a capability trait the embedder implements — so no feature here pulls in an
# HTTP client, a browser protocol, or a process spawner. `store` is on because
# the loop needs the durable model around a graph (versioned documents, run
# records, proposals) to have anything to iterate over.
tinyflows = { path = "vendor/tinyflows", version = "0.8.0", default-features = false, features = [
    "store",
] }
# The adaptive loop that lives beside the engine: select or author a graph, run
# it, judge the result, learn. `default-features = false` drops the bundled
# SQLite build so a backend is a deliberate choice rather than a default.
tinyflows-adaptive = { path = "vendor/tinyflows/crates/adaptive", version = "0.1.0", default-features = false }
# The durable agent + graph harness. Vendored as `vendor/tinyagents` and pinned
# by its gitlink like the others. Nothing in the module library needs it: it is
# an optional dependency behind the `tinyagents` feature of `crates/tinyloops`,
# switched on so an example can build a real harness around a loop. Default
# features off keeps the bundled SQLite checkpointer and the builtin tool family
# out of the graph until an example asks for them.
tinyagents = { path = "vendor/tinyagents", version = "2.1.1", default-features = false }
# Hashes the emitted loop graph into the signature a checkpoint records, so a
# resume against a graph whose topology has since changed is refused rather than
# restored into slots that no longer mean what they meant. Not
# `std::hash::DefaultHasher`: its output is documented as unstable across
# releases, so a signature built on it would refuse resumes after a toolchain
# bump rather than after a topology change. Only the SHA-256 digest is used, so
# no default feature is needed beyond the crate's own.
sha2 = "0.10"
# Derive macros for the crate-wide error type in `crates/tinyloops/src/error/`.
# Every dependency entry should carry a comment like this one saying why it is
# here.
thiserror = "2"
# The bus payload types are serialized into TinyBus frames.
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
# Positional argument arrays and the module configuration blob.
serde_json = "1"
# Module integration tests exercise the real asynchronous in-memory TinyBus.
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread", "time"] }

# Lints apply to every member that opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`, and
# to every target of that member. CI runs clippy with `-D warnings`, so anything
# set to "warn" here fails the build in CI.
[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"
missing_docs = "warn"
missing_debug_implementations = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"
rust_2018_idioms = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
# Library code must not panic on its own; tests and examples may.
unwrap_used = "warn"
expect_used = "warn"
panic = "warn"
todo = "warn"
unimplemented = "warn"
# Public fallible/panicking APIs must document their failure modes.
missing_errors_doc = "warn"
missing_panics_doc = "warn"
# Documentation hygiene.
doc_markdown = "warn"
# `#[must_use]` on pure public functions.
must_use_candidate = "warn"

[workspace.lints.rustdoc]
broken_intra_doc_links = "warn"
private_intra_doc_links = "warn"

[profile.release]
# Cross-crate optimization and smaller, faster binaries for release builds.
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = "debuginfo"

[package]
name = "tinyloops"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
description = "A loop engineering framework: the scaffolding for agentic loops that run a workflow, judge what came back, and decide whether to go round again."
documentation = "https://docs.rs/tinyloops"
readme = "../../README.md"
keywords = ["agent", "loop", "workflow", "tinyflows", "tinybus"]
categories = ["development-tools"]
publish = false

[lib]
# Keep the ordinary Rust library for tests and downstream reuse while also
# producing the native module artifact that TinyBus loads at runtime.
crate-type = ["rlib", "cdylib"]

[dependencies]
# The wire contract: member names, payload types, and the contract version.
# Re-exported wholesale from `src/lib.rs` so a consumer takes one dependency
# rather than two, and so `tinyloops::GreetRequest` and
# `tinyloops_bus::GreetRequest` are the same type.
tinyloops-bus = { workspace = true }
tinybus = { workspace = true }
# The workflow engine. `src/policy/ladder.rs` generates the jq the graph
# branches on and evaluates it through `tinyflows::expr`, which is how the Rust
# router and its jq translation are checked against each other rather than
# trusted to match. No engine feature beyond the workspace default is needed:
# nothing here runs a graph.
tinyflows = { workspace = true }
# `LoopState` is the loop's accumulator, and the accumulator crosses the graph
# as JSON. `derive` is the whole reason it is here.
serde = { workspace = true }
# The expression scope a ladder is evaluated against is a `serde_json::Value`,
# and the accumulator is serialized into it.
serde_json = { workspace = true }
# The graph signature of `src/loops/`: a SHA-256 over the emitted graph's node
# ids, kinds, ports, edges, and every rendered threshold.
sha2 = { workspace = true }
tinybus-module = { workspace = true }
thiserror = { workspace = true }
# Optional, and only ever reached from an example. The `tinyagents` feature
# below turns it on; the module library itself never calls into it, so a host
# that loads the `cdylib` resolves neither the harness nor its HTTP client.
tinyagents = { workspace = true, optional = true }

[dev-dependencies]
tokio = { workspace = true }
# `mock` is a dev-only addition on top of the dependency above: it supplies the
# in-memory capability implementations the loop examples run on, which is what
# keeps them offline and deterministic. A shipped module brings its own
# capabilities rather than the mocks, so the feature stays out of `[dependencies]`.
tinyflows = { workspace = true, features = ["mock", "testkit"] }
# Test-only. `tinyflows::interception::StepInterceptor` is declared with
# `#[async_trait]`, so implementing it — which `tests/loop_run.rs` does to prove
# a replayed activation changes no counter — needs the same macro. Already in
# the tree via the engine, and a dev-dependency so nothing the loader resolves
# gains it.
async-trait = "0.1"

[features]
default = []
# Pulls in the TinyAgents durable agent + graph harness so the examples that
# drive a loop from a harness can compile. Nothing in `src/` is gated on it —
# it exists to give an example a real harness instead of a hand-rolled stand-in.
tinyagents = ["dep:tinyagents"]

# Every other example is discovered from `examples/` and builds on a bare
# `cargo test`. This one additionally needs the optional crate above, and
# `required-features` is what keeps a default build from trying to compile it
# without one.
[[example]]
name = "tinyagents_harness"
path = "examples/tinyagents_harness.rs"
required-features = ["tinyagents"]

[lints]
workspace = true
